title: The Work of the Spirit vs the Law
english: As the universe abandons the practice of those hearing, our Lord Jesus Christ, through the gift of the Spirit, works the salvation of those under himself, acting as a creator who makes us from the beginning, transforming and regulating us to receive and dwell in the divine inspiration; he uses words for exhortation to prepare us fitly, shaping us with a spirit that provides, not by leaving things to us. For if we were judged again, we would be unable to obey, and the knowledge of sin would be among us rather than from us; rather, preparing us as vessels for the Spirit, he relaxes our compassion toward the world and loosens fleshly bonds while increasing our indwelling of the Spirit.

Thus the law is sharp for punishment and the Spirit is non-vengeful; the one seeks the uprightness of men toward justice, the other provides from himself. For the law follows the one, bringing punitive consequences to the commanding one when he is not obeyed, but the Spirit, having power for the correction of those who believe, even if the first ones receive the creation from him with weakness, does not immediately recognize or punish, but preserves the man being educated by the salvation from himself, just as Paul said Satan would deliver [one] to destruction of the flesh so that the spirit might be saved (1 Corinthians 5:5). For the Spirit of the Lord endures until the presence of Christ, until the time of the present creation expires, the standing of judgment where he casts away the uncorrectable and finds the rest fit for eternal life.

Therefore the apostle also says elsewhere that God is the one working in you, both to will and to work according to his good pleasure (Philippians 2:13), not cutting off our autonomy, but explaining the power from God toward virtue. And the Savior, having risen, breathed in the Holy Spirit, and therefore, dwelling in us, commanded us not to worry about what we shall speak, saying, 'It is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father speaking in you' (John 16:13).

Already the prophetic word, defining the new covenant in the gift of the Spirit, says, explaining the divine toward Israel in discourse: 'And this covenant is for them from me,' he said, 'and my Spirit is upon you, and the words which I have given into your mouth shall not depart from your mouth or from the seed of your mate,' says the Lord, 'from now and unto the age' (Isaiah 59:21). And these things are through Isaiah. But through Jeremiah, God promising the new covenant says: 'This is the covenant which I will make with them in those days,' he says, 'giving my laws into their hearts, and upon...'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG Fragmenta in epistulam ad Romanos u02-rem-early

title: The Law, Knowledge, and the Spirit
english: I will write them upon their mind, and no longer shall each one teach his neighbor, saying, 'Know the Lord,' for all shall know me from the least to the greatest of them, that I will be propitiatory toward their sins; [this is done by] promising the energy of the Spirit in these, through which also a propitiation is made by God, the lifting up of the thoughts of sin according to the law, while the spiritual unselfishness allows the propitiation to enter. And indeed, through Ezekiel, He promises to give a new heart and a new spirit for the fulfillment of our own wills.

Thus, the apostle rightly defines the life according to Christ in the things presented, saying that not in the letter is the power of sin against us made weak (Rom 7,8), since the Spirit does not come for the sake of its knowledge and its condemnation through this, but for the removal of sin and the energy of righteousness, which is not human but divine, just as it was said in the beginning that the righteousness of God is being revealed through the gospel. For those who have not heard the law, the knowledge of this approaches them, just as it was previously said that the Gentiles, not having the law, do the things of the law by nature, showing the work of the law written in their own hearts (Rom 2:15); but for those under the law, the letter of the law and the natural meaning stir up the thoughts, being convicted by the teacher so that they might be able to discern the good and the bad for themselves.

So understand this for me, he says, lest the law had been placed first, as now it is not possible for those who are still infants to understand, and there is no condemnation there (Rom 7,10); for ignorance is not subject to punishment. After these things, behold the commandment coming; there sin is astonished against us, the knowledge having come and the anger no longer dismissing itself against those things happening. In this way, sin indeed lives, gaining power and strength, but the man dies, being judged according to knowledge, and the command of the law, which gives life, stands around as a pretext for death; for without it, it is not possible for sin to be sin, nor to condemn man with death, because of this, the guilt of wickedness and the penalty of punishment are established.

All, he says, creation waits for us, and the time when we shall be seen in the glory due to us, as if nothing were more brilliant than the glory that will be about us (Rom 8). But creation falls to the sons of God, being God's possession; for the slave follows the free, and the possession is subject to the son because of his nobility. And the appropriation toward the Father subjects the slave to the sons. It is evident, then, that having grace, the sons are of God.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG Fragmenta in epistulam ad Romanos u02-rem-mid

title: The Glory of Creation and the Sorrow of the Elect
english: Because of the transformation of the Spirit, as he has previously stated, we have grace in having the ruling principle in creation, receiving the glory of the true Son; so that it is not beyond glory that such a great and such a creation should be subjected to men, who appear small in creation.

He has unloosed the elect from all accusations, and justification has pre-ordained the condemnation (Rom 8:33-34); so that neither a condemning law, nor the rulers of this age, holding man by sin and drawing him through sin into the slavery of death, shall still be strong against us. But the terror of the law ceases, being overcome by the grace of Christ, and the wickedness of the rulers of this age is weakened by the goodness of Him who was slaughtered for us and voluntarily gave Himself up by the good pleasure of God and Father, even though a resurrection came upon Him, concealing death, and we no longer see Christ having died, but living and sitting at the Father's side, and interceding for men according to the human, through which also He was joined to men, uniting what was divided.

From the hoped-for good things, both extremes have proceeded (Rom 9:1-5): the contention regarding love and the lamentation regarding those who have fallen away. For those being benefited love, but those failing in the benefits lament appropriately. He says, intensifying with divine testimony, that he does not speak only in word but also in disposition and truth, that he has the greatest sorrow continually present for his kinsmen. Let no one disbelieve, he says, if I lament concerning the adversaries and persecutors, nor let it be considered paradoxical if I desired to suffer the greatest things on their behalf, being handed over unto death by Christ.

For how is it not a pity that they hear men—those who are near them, even their own people—who have been called sons of God from the beginning, and have been glorified with glory from God in the world, and have received the covenant concerning bodily laws previously, and now have the second one having come regarding spiritual things in their hands, and those chosen for the worship of God and the promises of future good things, the [fathers] of the saints and God-loving ones, those homogeneous with the flesh of the Lord, these being cast off and despised and having fallen now into the greatest shame and lowliness. But therefore, even if what happened concerning them is worthy of lamentation, it is worthy to bless the God who thus judged, the Master over all, to whom all blessing is justly returned from all and upon all. And indeed, even regarding the most holy judgments, neither because the due justice of those being judged will appear manifest, nor because they are being turned away from Him by their prior intimacy with God, [...]
